description:
CaptivateIQ is transforming the way companies plan, manage, and optimize sales performance. We started by revolutionizing incentive compensation management, and now we're expanding our platform to solve broader sales planning challenges. Recognized by industry analysts like Forrester and G2 and backed by top-tier investors, including Sequoia, ICONIQ, Accel, and Sapphire Ventures,  we empower high-growth companies like Netflix, Figma, and Stripe with the flexibility and insights needed to drive revenue performance.

 

Join a talented, fast-growing team committed to solving some of the most complex and impactful problems in sales performance management.

 

About the Role

Enterprise and mid-market buyers now arrive at the conversation further along than they used to. They have done AI-assisted research, formed strong opinions, and many believe they can build what they need themselves. A demand engine designed for the 2022 buyer will not reach them.

We are hiring a demand generation leader to rebuild ours for this buyer, and to run it on AI-native workflows rather than bolting automation onto the old playbook. You will own the integrated campaign, ABM, nurture, and paid programs that create and accelerate pipeline for CaptivateIQ's compensation, planning, and AI agents products. You will lead a team, work hands-on in the work, and be accountable for pipeline that converts, not just leads that count.

This is a player-coach role. You set the strategy, you build with your team, and you decide where AI replaces manual work and where human judgment stays.

 

What you'll own

  • Pipeline and funnel economics

    • Own the demand generation pipeline and qualified opportunity targets across mid-market and enterprise, with a clear forecast and the levers to close any gap.

    • Hold the team to funnel economics, not volume: lead-to-opportunity conversion, win rate on marketing-sourced pipeline, cost per SQO, and pipeline accelerated on open opportunities.

    • Make the call on what to cut, scale, or test, using performance data rather than attachment to a program.

    An AI-native demand engine

    • Operate AI-first. Build and maintain the team's AI playbook: documented workflows, prompts, and agents (Claude and similar tools) for campaign briefs, audience and list building, asset production, reporting, and call and market-signal analysis.

    • Measure it. Treat each AI workflow like a program: a hypothesis, a baseline, a measured efficiency or conversion gain, and a decision to scale or kill it.

    • Reach the AI-era buyer. Adapt how we reach buyers who research in LLMs, not search: AEO and AI-citation visibility, ungated assets that earn trust, and intent signals tied to AI, build-vs-buy, and competitor research.

    • Stay skeptical. Keep us honest about where AI is doing real work and where it adds noise, in our own marketing and in what we say to customers.

    Integrated campaigns, ABM, and nurture

    • Run quarterly campaign planning with Product Marketing, Content, Creative, Field, and Sales to turn product launches and market narratives into multi-channel programs across email, paid, events, direct mail, webinars, and content.

    • Design and run ABM across 1:1, 1:few, and 1:many, using buying-stage and signal data (for example UserGems and intent tools) to swarm priority accounts alongside BDRs and AEs.

    • Build nurture that moves known contacts and open-opportunity buying groups toward a meeting, with a measured conversion rate from lead to MQL to opportunity.

    • Tailor programs to segment, vertical, and persona, including finance and total-rewards buyers alongside our traditional RevOps and comp audiences.

    Partnership with BDR, Sales, and Field

    • Share one pipeline plan with BDR leadership: program-level enablement, follow-up sequences, response SLAs, and a standing feedback loop on lead and meeting quality.

    • Make marketing useful in the sales cycle: warm openers for AE accounts, content for late-stage and competitive deals, and build-vs-buy narratives that sales can use.

    • Coordinate with Field and Events so the event pipeline is planned, followed up, and measured end to end.

    Measurement and operating rhythm

    • Work with Marketing Operations on attribution, funnel reporting, and program-level dashboards the whole GTM team trusts.

    • Lead monthly program reviews and quarterly campaign retros, and turn what you learn into the next quarter's plan.

    • Translate performance data into clear recommendations for marketing and sales leadership.

    Your team

    • Lead and develop a team of campaign and program managers, set clear priorities and ownership, and coach to a high standard of execution.

    • Raise the team's AI fluency so that every role runs faster with AI and can show the result.

What success looks like

  • First 6 months

    • Within 30 days: you understand the funnel, the buyer, and the current programs; you have met BDR, Sales, PMM, and MOPs counterparts; you have a clear read on what is working.

    • Within 90 days: you own the pipeline forecast and a quarterly plan; your first AI-assisted workflows are live with baselines; BDR follow-up on programs is measurably tighter.

    • Within 6 months: pipeline and funnel conversion are trending to target, the team runs on a documented AI playbook with proven gains, and ABM and nurture programs are producing meetings and accelerated opportunities.

What you bring

  • 7+ years in B2B demand generation at a high-growth SaaS company, with a record of meeting or exceeding pipeline targets (not only MQL targets).

  • Experience leading people or leading through others; comfortable managing 1–2 directs and working hands-on.

  • Hands-on use of AI in marketing work. You can describe a specific workflow you built with Claude, GPT, or similar tools, what it replaced or sped up, and how you measured it.

  • A point of view on where demand generation is heading, backed by things you have tested, rather than one fixed playbook.

  • Strong command of integrated campaign planning, ABM, and nurture, and of the metrics that tell you whether each is working.

  • Working knowledge of a modern stack: a CRM (Salesforce), marketing automation (HubSpot or Marketo), ABM and intent tools (such as UserGems, 6sense, G2  or Bombora), and project management.

  • Clear written and verbal communication, including the ability to present results to senior leaders.

  • A close working style with BDR and Sales teams, with direct feedback in both directions.

Nice to have

  • Experience marketing to RevOps, finance, HR, or total-rewards buyers, or to buyers in a build-vs-buy decision.

  • Experience with AEO or LLM-referral measurement, paid media, or field and event programs.

  • Experience in a multi-product or land-and-expand motion.

How we work

  • Bias toward action. You act on good information quickly and do not wait for perfection.

  • Operate with clarity. You know the goal of every program and report on it plainly, including what did not work.

  • Be an owner. You own the number and hold yourself and others accountable to it.

  • Deliver impact. You measure progress, learn from misses, and push for outcomes that matter to the business.

  • Lead with empathy. You seek to understand stakeholders first and give feedback that helps people grow.

Why this role

  • You will shape how a company in a fast-changing category finds and wins buyers. You will have real autonomy to bring in what has worked elsewhere, access to a modern stack, and a team that already works with AI daily. You will sit at the center of marketing, BDR, sales, and product marketing, with direct visibility to company leadership.

Benefits

  • Comprehensive Healthcare: 100% coverage for medical, dental, and vision for all FTEs, with roughly 75% coverage for dependents.

  • Flexible Time Off: Flexible vacation days plus quarterly mental health days to ensure you have the space to recharge.

  • Annual Stipends: Dedicated funds for your professional development and caretaking needs.

  • Work Anniversary Bonuses: Annual bonuses to celebrate your milestones and contributions to the CaptivateIQ team that grow as your tenure does.

  • Retirement Savings (US-Only): A 401(k) plan to help you invest in and secure your future.

  • Premium Tools: The latest Apple hardware to empower you to do your best work.

  • Inclusive Community: Active Employee Resource Groups (ERGs) that celebrate shared identities and support our DEI goals by fostering an environment where diverse talent thrives.

Notice for Prospective Candidates

  • Only emails from @captivateiq.com should be trusted.

We are aware of active recruitment scams using the CaptivateIQ name, in which individuals pose as our recruiters and post fake remote job openings and make fake job offers on the Internet. Please note, we will never do the following:

  • Attempt to correspond with a candidate using a free web-based account, such as an email address that ends in @gmail.com, @yahoo.com, @hotmail.com, etc.

  • Make an offer of employment without conducting multiple rounds of interviews face-to-face using secure video-conferencing technology.

  • Ask candidates to cash checks to buy equipment on behalf of CaptivateIQ.

  • Ask candidates to make a payment in order to be considered for a position.

  • Make early requests for candidates' personal information such as date of birth, passport details, credit card numbers, bank details and social security number, etc.

  • Please note that we’ll only ask for more sensitive personal information in connection with background checks after an offer is made.

CaptivateIQ participates in E-Verify, web-based system that allows enrolled employers to confirm the eligibility of their employees to work in the United States
